parole.testo: Borrowed from Middle Low German bōnen, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *bʰeh₂- (“to shine”). Cognate with Dutch boenen.

parole.significato: to fumble (idly touch or nervously handle)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Middle Low German fummelen, fimmelen, perhaps ultimately imitative of fumbling. Or, from Proto-Indo-European *pal- (“to shake, swing”), see also Latin palpō (“to pat, touch softly”), and possibly Proto-Germanic *fōlijaną (“to feel”). Cognate with English fumble.

From Middle High German kil, which is possibly a borrowing from the north, from Middle Low German quiele, possibly ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *gʷelH- (“to pierce, stick”). Compare somewhat later Lower Rhine Middle Dutch kijl. See quill for more.

parole.significato: score, a set of twenty, e.g. of sheaves, livestock, eggs
parole.testo: From Middle Low German stîge, from Old Saxon stīga (“set of twenty”). Cognate with Middle Dutch stîge, Crimean Gothic stega. Has been compared to Ancient Greek στίχος (stíkhos, “row, line”), which if related, from Proto-Indo-European *steygʰ- (“to walk, go, ascend”).

parole.significato: to warn, to make aware of danger
parole.testo: 15th century, from Middle Low German wārschûwen (“to warn, make aware”). Cognate with Dutch waarschuwen.
